intro.data: Trace each user to their email, that email's host, the host's domain, and the domain's registrar — FOUR steps, each in a box, each able to fail. The tray holds the four steps and bind machines (faithful and impostor); bring the right ones onto the board and wire ONE pipeline. FIVE cases keep you honest: Ada is complete; Bo has no email; Cy has an email but no host; Di has a host but no domain; Eve has a domain but NO registrar — so the pipeline must reach Ada's registrar yet short-circuit to Nothing for the other four, never inventing anything. Watch the last bind: one impostor only fabricates when the emptiness appears at the FINAL step, so checking the shallow failures alone will pass a liar.
intro.alchemy: Trace each herb to its essence, that essence's salt, the salt's crystal, and the crystal's seal — FOUR steps, each in a vial, each able to come up empty. The tray holds the steps and decant apparatus (faithful and impostor); bring the right ones and wire ONE line. FIVE cases: Sage is complete; Rue has no essence; Cress has essence but no salt; Dill has salt but no crystal; Elder has a crystal but NO seal — so the line must reach Sage's seal yet stay empty for the other four. Watch the last decant: one impostor only invents when the emptiness lands at the FINAL step.
intro.spellcraft: Trace each rune to its omen, that omen's sign, the sign's fate, and the fate's seal — FOUR steps, each in a charm, each able to fizzle. The tray holds the workings (faithful and impostor); bring the right ones and wire ONE weave. FIVE cases: Ash is complete; Bramble has no omen; Cinder has an omen but no sign; Dusk has a sign but no fate; Ember has a fate but NO seal — so the weave must reach Ash's seal yet stay dark for the other four. Watch the last working: one impostor only fakes when the dark lands at the FINAL step.
intro.abstract: Just x means the value x is present; Nothing means absent; bind runs the next step on a Just but passes Nothing straight through. From the tray bring four Kleisli arrows and wire A through T(B), T(C), T(D) to T(E). Five inputs short-circuit at different depths (full success, then Nothing arising at step 1, 2, 3, and 4); a faithful chain passes all five. Each impostor fabricates on some short-circuit case — and the step-4 impostor passes the success and the step-1/2/3 failures, betraying itself ONLY when emptiness first arises at step 4. Leave them behind.

afterSuccess.data: One pipeline, five outcomes: Ada reached her registrar, while Bo, Cy, Di, and Eve each short-circuited to Nothing at exactly the step their data ran out — no invented host, domain, or registrar anywhere. The dangerous impostor was 'Invent Registrar': it passed Nothing through correctly and read Ada's real registrar, so it sailed past the success AND the first three failures; it betrayed itself only on Eve, whose domain genuinely has no registrar — the DEEPEST empty case. That's the whole point of a monad: bind threads 'might be empty' through every step, so failure propagates honestly by construction — and it is why the suite tests every failure depth, not just the shallow ones.
afterSuccess.alchemy: One line, five outcomes: Sage reached its seal, while Rue, Cress, Dill, and Elder stayed empty exactly where the matter ran out. 'Invent Seal' passed empty through and read Sage's real seal, so it slipped past the success and the first three failures — and betrayed itself only on Elder, the deepest empty. That's a monad: bind threads 'might be empty' through every step.
afterSuccess.spellcraft: One weave, five outcomes: Ash reached its seal, while Bramble, Cinder, Dusk, and Ember stayed dark exactly where the thread ran out. 'Cast Seal's' impostor passed dark through and read Ash's real seal, so it slipped past the success and the first three failures — and betrayed itself only on Ember, the deepest dark. That's a monad: bind threads 'might fizzle' through every step.
afterSuccess.abstract: bind threaded ∅ through the four-arrow chain, so the composite short-circuited at the right depth for each input. The step-4 impostor passes Nothing through and agrees with the faithful bind on Just domain₁, so it clears the success and the depth-1/2/3 failures; it differs only on Just domain₅, the depth-4 empty, where it fabricates. The monad laws make this composition associative and unit-respecting — failure propagates by the laws, and only a suite covering every depth pins the behavior.

reveal.summary: A monad (a functor T with return η and bind/join μ obeying the unit and associativity laws) lets you chain steps that carry an effect — here 'might be empty' — so the effect threads through automatically. Testing every failure depth is what proves a long pipeline short-circuits instead of fabricating: an impostor can match the faithful bind on the success and every shallow failure and still invent a value when emptiness first appears at the last step.
reveal.moreFormal: The monad laws — left/right identity (bind ∘ return = id) and associativity of bind — guarantee a chain of binds means one unambiguous thing, however grouped. Optional, List, State, and Promise are all monads.
reveal.programmerAnalogy: user.flatMap(getEmail).flatMap(getHost).flatMap(getDomain).flatMap(getRegistrar) — one missing link anywhere yields None; nothing invented, even at the final hop.
